motif: Measurement made physical: every building carries a graduated scale (tick-marked bands or a brass rule line) plus one small turquoise gauge-light accent, and no flame anywhere. Only h014 has a closed ring; all other arcs and rings are open or segmented.

buildings.colour: pale cream limestone base with a bronze shaft
buildings.why: The one closed graduated ring on top is the hole in the silhouette. No other building has a closed ring.
A straight slatted shed with an open lattice porch is the longest and lowest mass in the race.

It keeps the chain's shed archetype and grows by one storey, a gable and a vane. The shade is darker than h08X because neighbours must not share a colour. The card asked for no recolor, so this is a deliberate departure.
The glass fume cupboard juts out as a box on a stalk from the two-bay hall. The turquoise vent glow sits inside it.
A corner drum with a clock face and a pulsing roof tank. Coral is the warm outlier of the race.
Two brass posts hold an open, segmented landing arc, which reads as a gate. The arc is open so it never competes with h014's closed ring.

buildings.colour: ivory bone-white columns with a gold urn
buildings.why: The open pavilion of slender columns under a flat span is the only openwork building. Gold is its single declared exception.
The stepped gable and guild body form a stepped mass. The sword monument and turquoise yard flag are the accents.
It grows the h00T stepped mass with a low copper dome, a colonnade and twin crossed swords. The patina separates it from the grey base.

buildings.colour: dull ochre brass with ink-teal trim
buildings.why: An open gantry shed with the proof rail and painted scale radiating across the yard gives a low, spread-wing footprint.
A squat, shoulder-broad stepped column with a full-height glass slit. It is thicker than the Nightelf spires.
A two-storey tiered institute with a gnomon yard and a vent in place of a spire. The blue panels are the Academy blue.

buildings.colour: dark ink-teal shaft with a pale glass beacon and brass armillary
buildings.why: It stacks the school's terraces into a tall turned shaft with a lit dome and an open, turning armillary. Its colour differs from h09X, and the open rings keep h014's ring unique.
